title: Emrys and the Vow
premise: Marine biologist Coral Dravenmoor has spent a decade avoiding love after a betrayal she never fully named, burying herself in sea turtle conservation on a remote island. When a freak snowstorm traps her with her estranged ex-fiancé, Julian, and his business partner — the rival who helped break them apart — old wounds and long-buried truths surface. As the storm isolates them for weeks, Coral must untangle what really happened in their twenties, forgive herself for the vow of solitude she made, and choose whether inheritance means repeating the past or building something new. She ends the book not by returning to an old love, but by founding a chosen family research station with the person who stayed.
about_author: Yara Voss is the pen name of a former field researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters and now writes love stories set where the weather refuses to cooperate. She lives near the coast with two rescue dogs and an unreasonable number of unfinished notebooks.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On Ashen Cay, Coral logs nesting turtles and deflects her assistant's questions about why she never dates. Establishes her ritualized isolation and quiet competence. Emotional beat: contentment that is secretly avoidance.

chapters.title: The Letter That Smells Like Winter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A legal letter arrives: her late mentor left her half of a mainland research trust — co-owned by someone named J. Whitlock. Her hands shake. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: Julian
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. In the city, Julian learns the same news and realizes 'Dravenmoor' can only be Coral. His partner, Theo, urges him to contest it. Emotional beat: guilt he's spent ten years repackaging as resentment.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral travels to the mainland to sign papers before the trust dissolves; forecasters predict a historic snowstorm. She tells herself it's one meeting, one signature, one day. Emotional beat: braced resolve.

chapters.title: Two Rivals at a Dead End Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Snow closes the pass; Coral arrives at the trust's property to find Julian already there — and Theo's car sliding into the ditch behind hers. Three people, one house, no exits. Emotional beat: trapped recognition.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Their Twenties
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Over forced tea, the history leaks out: Coral and Julian were engaged at twenty-five; Theo was Julian's best friend whose interference ended it. Nobody says what actually happened. Emotional beat: old fire under new frost.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo proposes civil terms: shared chores, no past talk. Privately, Theo is terrified — they've loved both of them for a decade and engineered this trip hoping for exactly this. Emotional beat: hope laced with self-loathing.

chapters.title: Power Out
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The storm kills the power. Candles, cold rooms, and Julian fixing the generator with the same competence she once loved. Emotional beat: involuntary tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian finds Coral's old notebook in the study — her account of the broken engagement, pages torn out. He realizes she never knew the full truth either. Emotional beat: protective panic.

chapters.title: Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers Julian holding the notebook and realizes the torn pages are the ones Theo wrote — a confession letter from ten years ago that was never delivered. Emotional beat: cornered honesty approaching.

chapters.title: Snowed-In Truce
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The three cook together; laughter ambushes Coral mid-sentence. For one evening it feels like the family none of them had. Emotional beat: dangerous belonging.

chapters.title: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confronts Theo privately about the engagement's end; Theo admits lying to Coral back then but won't say why. Julian's anger curdles into suspicion of himself. Emotional beat: guilt re-examined.

chapters.title: Nesting Instinct
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral finds the property's abandoned hatchery records — her mentor had been quietly funding all three of them for years, betting they'd reunite. Emotional beat: feeling played, then strangely moved.

chapters.title: Mirror Work
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Alone, Coral finally names her own role: she walked away without asking questions because asking risked learning she wasn't enough. Emotional beat: the beginning of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Julian's Confession
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian tells Coral he called off the wedding because he believed she deserved someone who hadn't doubted her — a doubt planted by an anonymous letter. Emotional beat: grief shared is grief halved.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Letter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral remembers receiving one too, claiming Julian had been unfaithful. Both letters, same handwriting. They look at each other and say the name together: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They confront Theo in the snow-covered greenhouse. Theo breaks: the letters were lies meant to keep them apart — because Theo couldn't bear losing either of them. Emotional beat: raw, ugly, human confession.

chapters.title: Exile by Choice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo packs to walk into the storm rather than be forgiven. Coral stops them at the door: 'You don't get to decide you're unforgivable. That was my job.' Emotional beat: mercy as confrontation.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Uneasy peace. Coral admits to Julian she doesn't know if she loves him or loves who they were. He agrees to find out slowly. Emotional beat: honest uncertainty replacing fantasy.

chapters.title: The Trust's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Reading the trust documents, Julian finds a condition: the inheritance only holds if the three co-owners run the station together for one year. Their mentor engineered everything. Emotional beat: outrage softening into awe.

chapters.title: Roads Reopen
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The plows come; the world returns. Each must choose: leave, or stay. Coral drives to the road's end and sits there a long time. Emotional beat: choice made visible.

chapters.title: Coral Stays
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral turns around — not for Julian, she insists, but for the turtles, the station, the work. Everyone lets her have the fiction. Emotional beat: self-deception with good intentions.

chapters.title: Learning Each Other Again
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Montage-like chapter: rebuilding the station through spring. Small discoveries — Julian now hates coffee, Coral now laughs easily. Emotional beat: strangers becoming familiar.

chapters.title: Theo's Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo asks for boundaries: friendship only, no more manipulation, and the right to leave if it hurts too much. Coral and Julian agree. Emotional beat: fragile new contract.

chapters.title: First Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The team tags their first nest together; a local volunteer group joins, and the station gains its first found-family members beyond the three. Emotional beat: purpose larger than romance.

chapters.title: Old Habits
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Under stress, Julian withdraws into silence — the exact pattern that doomed them before. Coral calls it out immediately instead of enduring it. Emotional beat: breaking inherited patterns.

chapters.title: The Fight That Doesn't End Them
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their first real fight as adults: loud, honest, survivable. Afterwards, Julian says, 'We just did the thing we used to be incapable of.' Emotional beat: conflict as intimacy.

chapters.title: Coral's Mother Calls
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's mother reveals family history: generations of Dravenmoor women who chose solitude and called it strength. Coral sees the vow she inherited. Emotional beat: inheritance interrogated.

chapters.title: Breaking the Vow
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At her mentor's grave, Coral reads her own old vow of solitude aloud, then tears the page into the wind. Emotional beat: ceremony of release.

chapters.title: Julian Asks Nothing
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian, seeing Coral change, deliberately does not propose or push — he tells her he'd rather lose the timing than rush her. Emotional beat: love as patience.

chapters.title: Theo's Departure Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo submits resignation, convinced the year's end means exile. Coral finds the letter first. Emotional beat: fear of being the third wheel made literal.

chapters.title: Three Chairs
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral refuses the resignation: the station needs three directors, and she needs both of them — not as rivals for her heart, but as its architecture. Emotional beat: redefining the triangle.

chapters.title: Summer Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A hurricane forces another lockdown — mirroring chapter five. This time they face it as partners. Old trauma echoes, new responses. Emotional beat: history rhyming, then resolving.

chapters.title: Hatchlings
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The first tagged nest hatches at dawn; all three watch the turtles race the gulls. Coral realizes she stopped counting heartbreaks months ago. Emotional beat: quiet joy.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian finally asks Coral what she wants — not offers, not vows, just the question. Coral answers honestly: she wants to try, out loud, in daylight. Emotional beat: desire claimed without shame.

chapters.title: Renewal, Not Return
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral and Julian begin again deliberately — first date, first kiss, ten years older and unrecognizable in the best way. Emotional beat: new love wearing old faces.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The trust's lawyers arrive to verify the year's condition; a hostile outside buyer challenges the station's viability. External threat unites the trio. Emotional beat: siege mentality, shared.

chapters.title: Standing Ground
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Public hearing: volunteers, locals, and data defend the station. Coral speaks about inheritance as stewardship, not ownership. They win. Emotional beat: found family testifying for itself.

chapters.title: One Year Later
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The anniversary of the snowstorm. The three sign the permanent charter; Julian gives Coral not a ring but a key — to a home built for three plus whoever comes next. Emotional beat: full-circle transformation.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. They name a newly protected cove 'Emrys' — her mentor's first name, meaning 'ambition' and 'guardian.' Coral writes a new vow: to stay, to build, to belong. Final line mirrors the opening: she counts turtles now, but never instead of anything. Emotional beat: peace earned.
